document_summary: San Francisco Rent Board overview page explaining that landlords need one of 17 enumerated just-cause reasons under Rent Ordinance Section 37.9(a) to evict tenants in covered units in San Francisco, CA.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a))
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for the eviction; 17 enumerated reasons are allowed, and expiration of a lease or change in ownership is not just cause.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for one of 17 enumerated just causes (Section 37.9(a))
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including some units exempt from rent increase limits: newly constructed units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under Costa-Hawkins, and some tenancies where rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.interaction: Applies even to some tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limits (e.g., Costa-Hawkins-exempt units); state just cause law is not discussed in this document.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.extraction_notes: Official SF Rent Board summary page; effective date not stated in the document, so null. Relocation-assistance amounts are not covered in this document.
